mainEntity.name: How much does a Mazda 3 1.5 Skyactiv-D engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A used Mazda 3 1.5 Skyactiv-D engine (S5-DPTS) costs £400-£1,200 supply-only, while a reconditioned unit is £1,200-£2,200 and a full rebuilt engine £2,000-£3,800 [ESTIMATED]. Fitted costs add £390-£520 labour at a specialist. Compare quotes through EnginesMarket to find the best deal for your exact year and mileage.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of DPF problems in a Mazda 3 1.5 Skyactiv-D?

acceptedAnswer.text: Symptoms include excessive black smoke from the exhaust, a DPF warning light on the dashboard, reduced power or limp mode, and the car going into regeneration mode frequently . If a new DPF fills up very quickly after replacement, check the injectors - failing injectors can cause soot overload .

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mazda 3 1.5 Skyactiv-D?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt S5-DPTS engine costs around £2,000-£3,800 supply-only [ESTIMATED]. For a 2016-2018 Mazda 3 1.5 Skyactiv-D worth £6,000-£12,000, replacement is typically financially sensible - especially with a 12-month warranty. Always factor in labour (£390-£520) and the value of the car.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Mazda 3 1.5 Skyactiv-D engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A specialist workshop typically completes a full S5-DPTS engine swap in 8-10 hours. With parts sourcing and delivery factored in, allow 2-3 days from quote to car back on the road. Supply & fit options through EnginesMarket streamline the process by pairing you with a specialist who has the engine in stock.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Mazda 3 1.5 Skyactiv-D and the 2.2 Skyactiv-D?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.5-litre Skyactiv-D produces 105hp and 270Nm, while the 2.2-litre produces 150hp and 380Nm . The 1.5 was introduced for the UK in December 2015, offering 74.3mpg and 99g/km CO2, making it significantly more economical than the 2.2 . The 2.2 is more powerful but has a worse reputation for timing chain and oil pickup issues.

mainEntity.name: Does the Mazda 3 1.5 Skyactiv-D have a timing belt or chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Mazda 3 1.5 Skyactiv-D (S5-DPTS) uses a timing chain, not a belt . This is confirmed by Mazda's workshop manual and aftermarket catalogues from Gates and Dayco . The chain is designed to last the life of the engine with correct oil and regular servicing. Listen for rattling on cold start and check for P1336 codes as early warning signs .

historyTimeline.h2: Mazda 3 1.5 Skyactiv-D - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mazda 3 1.5 Skyactiv-D was introduced to the UK market in December 2015 as the most fuel-efficient diesel in the BM/BN-generation Mazda 3 range . Already established in the Mazda2 and CX-3, the 1.5-litre diesel offered 105hp and an impressive 74.3mpg combined, making it a compelling choice for high-mileage drivers .

milestones.description: 1.5 Skyactiv-D introduced in Mazda 3 (BM/BN generation) from 1 December, offering 105hp and 270Nm torque
Engine codes S5-DPTS and S5-DPTR, 1,498cc, 77kW (105hp), 99g/km CO2 with manual transmission
Production continues; engine codes S5Y7 and S5Y8 also used
End of 1.5 Skyactiv-D production; replaced by 1.8 Skyactiv-D in the BP-generation Mazda 3 from January 2019

commonProblems.h2: Mazda 3 1.5 Skyactiv-D Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mazda 3 1.5 Skyactiv-D (S5-DPTS) is a high-efficiency diesel with a timing chain, but it has known weak points that can drive replacement decisions: DPF blockage, P1336 timing chain/sensor codes, and injector issues. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: DPF Blockage & Regeneration Failure - Why the Mazda 3 1.5 Skyactiv-D DPF Fails
problems.rootCause: The 1.5 Skyactiv-D's DPF can fail to regenerate properly, particularly if the car is used for short urban journeys where the exhaust doesn't reach the required temperature for active regeneration . Reported symptoms include excessive black smoke, DPF warning lights, and limp mode .

problems.recommendation: For a 1.5 Skyactiv-D, regular motorway driving (30+ minutes at 2,000rpm+) allows passive regeneration and extends DPF life . If DPF issues persist, check injector condition - faulty injectors can cause soot overload that kills a new DPF quickly .

problems.h4: P1336 Timing Chain & Sensor Codes - Why the Mazda 3 1.5 Skyactiv-D Triggers Diagnostic Codes
problems.rootCause: The 1.5 Skyactiv-D uses a timing chain intended to last the life of the engine with proper maintenance . However, P1336 fault codes (crankshaft/camshaft correlation) can appear - while often initially diagnosed as timing chain stretch, they can also be caused by faulty crankshaft sensors, camshaft sensors, or exhaust pressure sensors that affect the fuel-air ratio .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic scan, sensor testing, replace CKP/CMP or exhaust pressure sensors
repairOptions.longevity: First port of call; often resolves P1336 without chain work
When genuine chain stretch is confirmed via elongation measurement
When chain failure has caused valve/piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2016-2018 Mazda 3 1.5 Skyactiv-D with 60k-100k miles is worth approximately £6,000-£12,000 [INDUSTRY ESTIMATE].
problems.recommendation: Before replacing the timing chain on a 1.5 Skyactiv-D, ensure a proper diagnostic check is performed . Many garages immediately diagnose P1336 as chain stretch, but sensor issues (CKP, CMP, exhaust pressure) can trigger the same code . If chain stretch is confirmed (via elongation angle measurement), replacement is necessary - but if sensor-related, repair is significantly cheaper .
